integrity_notes: All universal convergence claims are supported by an analytic logit-distance argument; finite symbolic and numerical diagnostics are supplemental. Autonomous fixed-point convergence and supercritical period-two attractors are credited to earlier literature, not claimed as novel. Literature priority is provisional; no independent scientific validation.
scientific_limitations: Applies to a two-strategy discrete replicator map with fixed normalized learning intensity and prescribed target sequence; arbitrary-input synchronization needs target values bounded away from 0 and 1. At the endpoint, convergence under nonconstant periodic forcing is exponential but under the centered constant forcing is generically inverse square-root. No assertion of a uniform exponential rate over all target sequences or of network-scale dynamics.
title: A sharp universal entrainment threshold for periodically driven replicator maps
